newsitem.title: UK: CBI chief says UK better off in EMU longer term.
newsitem.headline: CBI chief says UK better off in EMU longer term.

text.p: Britain would be better off inside European currency union than outside in the longer term, Adair Turner, director-general of the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Tuesday.

But, if European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) goes ahead as planned on January 1, 1999, there is a good argument for the UK to wait until growth in continental Europe caught up with it, he added.

"It's not in Britain's interests to go it alone. It is much better (for Britain) to be inside it than outside it," said Turner, speaking in London at Global 24, a conference on (EMU) linking participants around the world by video.
Turner said British businesses had supported the UK joining a single currency in the longer term but added it was important EMU was successful.
"Fudging...would make it less likely to be," he said.

Turner said the euro could only be a success if it was launched in a "sound fashion and not in a mistaken one." He said ideally, economic convergence should be met and flexible labour markets introduced.
Turner said if EMU was successful, it should deliver higher growth for Europe.
